Del sensor a la pantalla: From the sensor to the screen
Empecé por los dos extremos a la vez. En: I started at both ends at once. In 2017 I was programming **PIC** microcontrollers in **C** —a traffic-light model driven by a PIC 18F2550, simulated in Proteus— and starting **Kriver SmartHome**, an idea for affordable home automation: switching lights, fans or appliances from the home WiFi network.
Ese proyecto se controlaba desde el nave: That project was controlled from the browser, so hardware alone was not enough: the interface had to be built too. In parallel I was building web applications with **PHP** and **JavaScript**, and in 2018 I published my own **MVC framework in PHP**. Building one is a direct way to understand what a framework solves.
Ver un sistema completo, del sensor a la: Seeing a whole system, from the sensor to the user's screen, before specializing in any single layer.
Kriver SmartHome ya contaba con el teléf: Kriver SmartHome already counted on the phone as a remote. In 2019 I completed SENA's specialization in mobile app development, and mobile became my day-to-day work.
Cuando el producto crece, la estructura: When the product grows, so does its structure
El móvil pasó a ser el trabajo diario. D: Mobile became my daily work. For four years I built **fintech** and **e-commerce** apps with **React Native**: products that grew with every release and where a bug had consequences for the people using them. A structure fit for a small app was no longer enough.
Ahí incorporé **patrones de diseño**, **: That is where I brought in **design patterns**, **Clean Architecture** and **DDD** to keep business rules apart from the interface. What I already knew about interfaces was the foundation; what was new was organizing the code so the team could keep building on it without starting over.
Fuera del trabajo seguí el mismo camino:: Outside of work I kept on the same path: native tests in **Swift** and **Kotlin**, a **TypeScript** CRUD with DDD, a **React** task manager with Cypress and Atomic Design, and full-stack applications with **Django**, **Docker** and third-party APIs. Each exercise carried an earlier lesson into another environment. That same year I started, in parallel, a Software Development technology degree at UNICUCES.

Un mismo periodo reunió tres necesidades: One period brought together three needs: an e-commerce app in **React Native** for another market, new features in a native **iOS** app, and a **Python** backend with **FastAPI** and **MongoDB**. I arrived with mobile experience and had to learn whichever layer each challenge required.
En ese backend, las consultas a MongoDB: In that backend, the MongoDB queries were the bottleneck. I refactored them and response times dropped significantly. Contributing there meant leaving the screen and understanding the data model, so the product could respond better.
En paralelo profundicé en iOS con **Swif: In parallel I went deeper into iOS with **SwiftUI**, **MVVM**, Combine and MapKit. It wasn't about adding another framework: it was about seeing how state, navigation and the split of responsibilities change when moving from a cross-platform solution to a native one, and being able to contribute to both.

**HotPlate** es una estación de soldadur: **HotPlate** is an SMD reflow soldering station: C firmware for an **ATmega16**, PI control with autotuning, a **KiCad** PCB, a 3D-printed enclosure and **HotPlate Studio**, a **Python** desktop app that talks to the board over USB.
Para animar iconos en su pantalla sin ag: To animate icons on its display without running out of memory I wrote a GIF-to-bytes converter. And to keep the logs of my applications and devices without handing them to a third party, I'm building **kLog** with **Go**, GraphQL, **PostgreSQL** and Redis.
